title: Sequence clustering confounds AlphaFold2
source: Science TLDR podcast episode 1 show notes (Schafer et al.)
one_line: A critical re-evaluation of AF-cluster, the MSA-sequence-clustering method for predicting metamorphic protein conformations with AlphaFold2, arguing its successes are not better than random MSA subsampling.
key_claims: AF-cluster's predictions of alternative conformations for metamorphic proteins are no more accurate than random MSA sampling.
AF-cluster misidentifies non-metamorphic proteins as metamorphic and predicts erroneous alternative conformations.
Confidence scores reported for AF-cluster-predicted structures are inconsistent/discrepant with the predicted conformations.
CF-random, which runs ColabFold on randomly subsampled MSAs, is proposed as a more reliable and computationally cheaper alternative.
The authors argue for rigorous validation, complementary experimental/computational approaches, and methodological transparency in fold-switching prediction.
limitations: No specific accuracy numbers, benchmark set sizes, or confidence-score values are reported in the material provided.
The comparison is limited to AF-cluster versus random MSA subsampling within AlphaFold2/ColabFold; other conformational sampling methods are not assessed here.
CF-random is presented as an alternative but no quantitative validation against experimental structures is given in the summary.
open_questions: A blinded benchmark on a curated set of experimentally confirmed fold-switching and non-fold-switching proteins comparing AF-cluster, CF-random, and random subsampling.
Whether any MSA-manipulation strategy can distinguish genuine metamorphic proteins from single-fold proteins with a calibrated confidence metric.
Experimental validation (e.g. NMR or cryo-EM) of conformations predicted only by CF-random and not by AF-cluster.
